title: The Beetle Ranks of Scarabex
story: Across the cracked salt flats marches Scarabex the Shell Marshal, leading armored beetles in perfect rows toward the orchard town. Mr 6 climbs a boulder and counts the formation rather than panicking. Then he plays his own drum in the beetles' marching rhythm — and a quarter of them turn and follow HIM instead.
question: The beetles march in 14 rows of 16, and then 1/4 of the whole swarm peels off to follow Mr 6's drum. How many beetles are still marching with Scarabex?
hint: Multiply rows by columns to find the whole swarm first, then figure out what one quarter of that swarm is.
victory: With 168 beetles left and a rival drummer stealing the beat, Scarabex threw down his baton and marched his ranks home. Mr 6 led his 56 new friends to the orchard, where they ate only the fallen apples.
imagePrompt: Neat glittering rows of armored beetles crossing pale salt flats under a wide sunset sky while a numeral-six knight drums on a boulder and a quarter of the swarm turns toward him.
solution: One quarter leaves: 224 ÷ 4 = 56 beetles peel off.
praise: Multiplying rows by columns was the perfect start - the last step was taking that quarter away from the swarm.
